note.question: When will competing ad-supported platforms impose exclusive contracts on content providers, how does exclusivity change creator compensation, and who gains or loses?
note.overview: Two competing ad-supported platforms simultaneously choose exclusivity policies and then revenue-sharing rates; content providers choose where to post and consumers choose a platform. The paper derives pure-strategy equilibria and endogenous platform incentives to impose exclusivity.

coverage.note: The existing independently audited model map was decomposed into Mini-style components and linked back to the page-preserving source extraction.

components.label: Subgame-perfect exclusivity equilibrium with symmetric pure-strategy revenue sharing
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Subgame-perfect exclusivity equilibrium with symmetric pure-strategy revenue sharing. Lemmas 1 and 2 give the unique symmetric pure-strategy outcomes in the nonexclusive and exclusive subgames. Comparing platform profit across those subgames yields Corollary 1: exclusivity is the first-stage equilibrium only for beta below the threshold beta_1.
